docs.title: Smarter Accessibility Through User Behavior
docs.text: Accessible web experiences should not depend solely on users discovering browser or operating system accessibility settings. Adaptive Accessibility helps identify interaction patterns and recommends accessibility improvements when they are most needed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Adaptive Accessibility is an open-source browser extension that analyzes user interaction patterns during web browsing and recommends personalized accessibility improvements based on internationally recognized accessibility standards and usability principles.

The project also serves as a practical case study that combines Requirements Engineering, Software Architecture, Human-Centered Design, and Digital Accessibility to explore how adaptive technologies can make the web more inclusive.

docs.title: Why Adaptive Accessibility?
docs.text:
Modern browsers and operating systems already provide a wide range of accessibility features. However, these resources often remain underused because many users are unaware of their existence, do not realize they could benefit from them, or find them difficult to configure.

Adaptive Accessibility proposes a complementary approach. Rather than expecting users to manually search for accessibility settings, the extension observes interaction patterns that may indicate usability barriers and recommends appropriate accessibility improvements when they are most relevant.

The goal is not to diagnose disabilities or replace assistive technologies. Instead, the extension helps users discover accessibility resources that may improve their browsing experience based on how they interact with web content.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The extension follows a behavior-driven recommendation workflow.

User browses a website
        │
        ▼
Interaction events are collected
        │
        ▼
Behavior patterns are analyzed
        │
        ▼
Accessibility rules are evaluated
        │
        ▼
Personalized recommendations are generated
        │
        ▼
User decides whether to apply them

All recommendations are optional. Users always decide whether to accept, ignore, or permanently disable each recommendation.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
Adaptive Accessibility is built upon five fundamental principles:

  1. User-Centered — Recommendations support users without interrupting their browsing experience.
  2. Privacy First — Interaction analysis should occur locally whenever possible, minimizing data collection.
  3. Transparency — Every recommendation is accompanied by a clear explanation of why it was suggested.
  4. Accessibility by Design — Recommendations are grounded in recognized accessibility standards such as WCAG and WAI-ARIA.
  5. User Autonomy — Users always remain in control and choose whether to apply each recommendation.

docs.title: Project Goals
docs.text:
Adaptive Accessibility aims to:

  • Promote more accessible and inclusive web experiences.
  • Promote greater accessibility for applications and users
  • Encourage proactive accessibility recommendations based on user interaction.
  • Demonstrate the practical application of accessibility standards such as WCAG.
  • Integrate Requirements Engineering, Software Architecture, Human-Centered Design, and Digital Accessibility into a single open-source project.
  • Build a modular and extensible browser extension capable of evolving with new accessibility recommendations over time.

docs.title: Open Source
docs.text:
Adaptive Accessibility is an open-source project developed for educational, research, and community purposes.

Contributions are welcome from developers, designers, accessibility specialists, researchers, and anyone interested in making the web more accessible.

docs.title: WCAG 2.2
docs.text: Topic Description Application in Adaptive Accessibility Principles (POUR) Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust. Provide the foundation for all accessibility recommendations in the extension. Conformance Levels A, AA, and AAA. The project will primarily use Level AA criteria. 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Ensures adequate contrast between text and background. Recommend contrast enhancement when low visual comfort is detected. 1.4.4 Resize Text Content must remain usable when enlarged. Detect frequent zoom usage and suggest increasing font size. 1.4.12 Text Spacing Allows customization of spacing between lines, words, and characters. Recommend increased spacing to improve readability. 2.1.1 Keyboard All functionality must be accessible through a keyboard. Detect predominant keyboard navigation and recommend related accessibility features. 2.4.7 Focus Visible Focused elements must have a clearly visible indicator. Recommend visual focus enhancement during navigation. 3.3 Input Assistance Helps users prevent and recover from errors. Future support for recommendations related to forms.

docs.title: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices
docs.text: Topic Description Application in Adaptive Accessibility Landmark Roles Defines the main regions of a webpage. Support the identification of interface structure. Keyboard Navigation Patterns Defines accessible interactions using the keyboard. Support the identification of keyboard navigation behavior. Accessible Widgets Defines accessible interactive components. Serve as a reference for future recommendations. Focus Management Defines how focus should be handled. Support recommendations related to visible focus.

docs.title: ISO 9241-210
docs.text: Topic Description Application in Adaptive Accessibility User-Centered Design The user should guide the entire development process. All recommendations will be centered on user needs. User Participation Users participate in decision-making processes. Users will always be able to accept or reject a recommendation. Iterative Process The system should continuously evolve. Recommendation rules may be refined throughout the project. User Experience Considers effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction. Used as a reference to evaluate the quality of recommendations.

docs.title: Nielsen's Usability Heuristics
docs.text: Heuristic Application in Adaptive Accessibility Visibility of System Status Explain to users why a recommendation was presented. User Control and Freedom Allow users to accept, reject, or disable recommendations. Consistency and Standards Maintain consistent recommendations across different websites. Recognition Rather Than Recall Use simple and objective language in recommendations. Flexibility and Efficiency of Use Adapt recommendations according to observed user behavior. Help and Documentation Clearly explain each recommended accessibility feature.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
Adaptive Accessibility aims to make web accessibility more proactive by helping users discover accessibility resources through their interaction patterns rather than relying exclusively on manual browser or operating system settings.

The project combines Requirements Engineering, Software Architecture, Human-Centered Design, and Digital Accessibility to investigate how behavior-driven recommendations can improve the web experience while preserving user autonomy and privacy.

docs.title: General Objective
docs.text: Develop a browser extension capable of identifying user interaction patterns and recommending accessibility adaptations based on recognized accessibility standards and usability principles.

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
The first version of Adaptive Accessibility includes:

  • Browser extension development.
  • Interaction event collection.
  • Behavior pattern analysis.
  • Accessibility recommendation engine.
  • Recommendation rules based on WCAG and usability principles.
  • User preference management.
  • Local data persistence.
  • Complete project documentation.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
The project does not include:

  • Medical diagnosis.
  • Disability classification.
  • Automatic accessibility adaptations without user consent.
  • Automatic modification of browser or operating system settings.
  • Collection of sensitive personal or health information.
  • Replacement of existing assistive technologies.

docs.title: Target Audience
docs.text: Adaptive Accessibility is intended for three primary audiences.

docs.title: End Users
docs.text:
Users who may experience accessibility barriers during web navigation, regardless of whether they identify themselves as people with disabilities.

Examples include:

  • Older adults using digital services.
  • Citizens accessing government portals.
  • Users who frequently zoom web pages.
  • Users who primarily navigate using the keyboard.
  • Users who experience reading difficulties due to the visual presentation of web content.
  • Users who encounter repetitive interaction problems during navigation.

docs.title: Software Professionals
docs.text:
• Software Developers
  • Software Architects
  • Requirements Engineers
  • UX/UI Designers
  • Accessibility Specialists

docs.title: Researchers and Students
docs.text: Researchers, educators, and students interested in Requirements Engineering, Software Architecture, Human-Computer Interaction, Usability, and Digital Accessibility.

docs.title: Personas
docs.text:
To better understand user needs and support the Requirements Engineering process, Adaptive Accessibility will define a set of representative personas based on realistic usage scenarios.

These personas will represent different user profiles, navigation behaviors, accessibility needs, and interaction contexts. They will support the elicitation of requirements, creation of user stories, validation of accessibility recommendations, and evaluation of the proposed solution.

Examples of scenarios to be represented include:

  • Older adults accessing government services.
  • Citizens using public service portals.
  • Users who frequently increase browser zoom.
  • Users who primarily navigate using the keyboard.
  • Users who experience reading difficulties caused by interface design.
  • Users interacting with educational, financial, healthcare, and e-commerce websites.

Each persona will describe the user's background, goals, behaviors, challenges, accessibility needs, and interaction patterns relevant to the project.

docs.text:
The project is based on internationally recognized standards and best practices in accessibility, usability, human-centered design, and requirements engineering.
